settings.heading: You already know. You just stopped noticing.
settings.body:
The squeeze test before you serve. The dull thud off the back glass. The point where you quietly start swinging harder to get the same ball back.

That is not your technique going. That is a ball at 7 PSI pretending to be a ball at 11.

A softer ball comes off the racket with less energy, so players compensate — and it is the compensation, not the ball, that your elbow eventually complains about.

settings.heading: Play
settings.body: Finish your match. The balls come off the court warm and already losing pressure.

settings.heading: Seal
settings.body: Drop up to four balls in, twist the cap, three pumps. Ten seconds, every time.

settings.heading: Check
settings.body: The gauge on the cap shows the pressure inside. No guessing. No trusting.

settings.heading: Ten seconds after every match
settings.body: There is no clever mechanism to learn. The tube holds a higher pressure than the ball, so the ball stops leaking into it.

settings.question: Do these actually work? I’ve heard they don’t.
settings.answer: Most don’t — they leak slowly and you never find out. That is exactly why we put a gauge on the cap: check it whenever you like. If it drops more than 1 PSI in 30 days, we replace it free.

settings.question: £59 is a lot for a tube.
settings.answer: It is about seven cans of balls. Most players who are on court twice a week spend that in four months.

settings.question: How long does it take to work?
settings.answer: Balls hold their pressure from the moment you seal the tube. For balls that have already gone soft, allow 24–48 hours to bring them back up.

settings.question: Will it fit my brand of balls?
settings.answer: It fits all standard padel and tennis balls. Capacity is four — a standard can is three, so you have room for a spare.

settings.question: What if I don’t like it?
settings.answer: Thirty days, full refund. Return it unused in its box and keep the overgrips.

settings.heading: Stop buying the same balls twice.
settings.body: Tube, three overgrips and a cloth — everything that keeps your gear match-ready, for £79.
